title: Improvements in or relating to work holding devices

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.quote: A magnetic work holder may be switched . " on " or " off " by rotating the generally cylindrical magnet 12 through 90 degrees in a casing 10 which has the holding surfaces divided into at least two pole
features.note: The reference describes a casing (housing) containing a rotatable magnet and pole regions (pole shoes) that form holding surfaces (workpiece contact surfaces).
features.refuted: The quote describes a rotating magnet, not a 'displaceable' one in the general sense asserted.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.quote: A magnetic work holder may be switched . " on " or " off " by rotating the generally cylindrical magnet 12 through 90 degrees in a casing 10
features.note: The magnet is displaceable by rotation between an 'on' (gripping) and 'off' (release) position.
features.refuted: The quote teaches rotation through 90 degrees, not displacement along a direction between positions.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: casing 10 which has the holding surfaces divided into at least two pole regions 20, 22 and 21, 23 by recesses 15, 16.
features.note: The casing (housing) has holding surfaces divided into pole regions, which function as pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.refuted: The quote describes pole regions on the casing, not separate pole shoes attached to the housing.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: In the " on " position, shown in Fig. 3, the flux circuit may be completed through surface 25 of magnetic material to retain the device or will retain magnetic material placed across faces 20, 22.
features.note: The pole regions (faces 20, 22) are part of the flux circuit, guiding the magnetic field to retain magnetic material (workpiece).

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: The reference describes a rotating magnet and pole faces, but does not specify any angles of the workpiece contact surface relative to the magnet's displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: While a magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes is disclosed, there is no mention of the contact surface angle relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.quote: In the " on " position, shown in Fig. 3, the flux circuit may be completed through surface 25 of magnetic material to retain the device or will retain magnetic material placed across faces 20, 22.
features.note: The device retains magnetic material (ferromagnetic workpiece) across the pole faces when in the 'on' (gripping) position, implying magnetic force.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: The reference describes a cylindrical magnet rotating within a casing, but does not specify a longitudinal axis for the housing or that the displacement direction is parallel to it.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.quote: The magnet 12 comprises pole faces 13, 14 with spaced ribs 26, 27 on its side faces, the ribs and pole faces being machined to fit in the bore 11.
features.note: The magnet itself has ribs and pole faces, which direct the field, but the pole shoes (pole regions 20, 22, 21, 23) are described as holding surfaces without specific active structures mentioned for directing the field.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles for an active structure on the pole shoes.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: The magnet 12 comprises pole faces 13, 14 with spaced ribs 26, 27 on its side faces, the ribs and pole faces being machined to fit in the bore 11.
features.note: The magnet has spaced ribs, which could be considered projections for directing the magnetic field, but these are on the magnet itself, not explicitly on the pole shoes that form the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: While the magnet has ribs, there is no description of adjacent projections on the pole shoes with a recess between them, nor any dimensional relationship between recess and projection length.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: The reference describes retaining magnetic material but does not mention any specific positioning device for the workpiece.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.quote: casing 10 which has the holding surfaces divided into at least two pole regions 20, 22 and 21, 23 by recesses 15, 16.
features.note: The division into at least two pole regions implies the creation of opposite poles (north and south) for magnetic attraction when the magnet is in the 'on' position.
features.refuted: The quote only mentions pole regions divided by recesses, not that the magnet makes one act as north and the other as south.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.quote: A magnetic work holder may be switched . " on " or " off " by rotating the generally cylindrical magnet 12 through 90 degrees in a casing 10
features.note: The magnet is mechanically displaceable by rotation.
features.refuted: The quote only describes rotation, with no mention of electrical, pneumatic, or mechanical displacement mechanisms.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference describes switching the magnet 'on' or 'off' but does not mention any sensors for detecting its position or the presence of a workpiece.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.note: The reference does not describe any receptacles in the housing for sensors or supply lines.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.note: The reference describes a magnetic work holder but does not mention any interface for attaching it to a manipulator.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.quote: In the " off" position the magnet is rotated through 90 degrees (Fig. 4, not shown) and the flux is short-circuited through the sides of the casing.
features.note: The casing itself acts as a shielding device by short-circuiting the flux in the 'off' position, preventing field escape to the workpiece.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference mentions ribs on the magnet but does not specify their length or relate it to workpiece thickness.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: The reference does not describe any receptacles in the form of a groove in the housing.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles for an active structure on the pole shoes.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles for an active structure on the pole shoes.

claims.quote: A magnetic work holder may be switched . " on " or " off " by rotating the generally cylindrical magnet 12 through 90 degrees in a casing 10 which has the holding surfaces divided into at least two pole
claims.note: The reference discloses a magnet arranged in a casing that is displaceable (rotatable) between an 'on' (gripping) and 'off' (release) position. However, it does not explicitly mention a 'displacement direction' as a linear movement, but rather a rotational movement.

claims.quote: A magnetic work holder may be switched . " on " or " off " by rotating the generally cylindrical magnet 12 through 90 degrees in a casing 10 which has the holding surfaces divided into at least two pole

claims.note: The reference does not describe any specific contact surface angle or its relation to a displacement direction.

claims.quote: A magnetic work holder may be switched . " on " or " off " by rotating the generally cylindrical magnet 12 through 90 degrees in a casing 10

claims.note: The pole faces and ribs act as an active structure to guide the magnetic field.

claims.note: This reference does not describe any bevels on the active structure or holding surfaces.
This reference does not describe any bevels or a bevel angle between a bevel and a workpiece contact surface.

However, it does not explicitly state they are for directing the magnetic field or forming the workpiece contact surface, as the workpiece contact is described as being across faces 20, 22 of the casing.

claims.note: This passage describes spaced ribs (projections) on the magnet, which can be interpreted as a first and second projection.

claims.quote: The magnet 12 comprises pole faces 13, 14 with spaced ribs 26, 27 on its side faces, the ribs and pole faces being machined to fit in the bore 11.
claims.note: The 'spaced ribs' imply that they are adjacent to one another on the side faces.
claims.refuted: Quote mentions spaced ribs on the magnet but does not teach that first and second projections are adjacent to one another.

claims.quote: The magnet 12 comprises pole faces 13, 14 with spaced ribs 26, 27 on its side faces, the ribs and pole faces being machined to fit in the bore 11.
claims.note: The term 'spaced ribs' implies that there are spaces or recesses between the ribs (projections).
